title: Russell Westbrook number retirement: OKC Thunder to hang No. 0 from the rafters in February - CBS Sports
description: Westbrook's number will go in the Paycom Center rafters on Feb. 7 when OKC hosts the Knicks
body:
Westbrook's number will go in the Paycom Center rafters on Feb. 7 when OKC hosts the Knicks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Oklahoma City Thunder will put Russell Westbrook's No. 0 into the rafters at the Paycom Center on Feb. 7, 2027, when they host the New York Knicks, the team announced on Monday.
Westbrook retired this offseason after an 18-year career that saw him make nine All-Star teams, nine All-NBA teams and win the 2016-17 MVP award. All but one of those All-Star and All-NBA seasons came as a member of the Thunder; he averaged 23.0 points, 8.4 assists, 7.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game across 821 appearances in an Oklahoma City uniform. "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," general manager Sam Presti said in a statement. "His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever."The Thunder traded Westbrook to the Houston Rockets before the 2019-20 season, but he struggled to stick with a team for long. While he remained productive, he bounced from Houston to Washington to Los Angeles (both the Lakers and Clippers) to Denver to Sacramento before calling it a career, never lasting two full seasons in the same place. After a rash of injuries in Oklahoma City and with Westbrook's retirement still fresh, some wondered if the Thunder might consider calling in Westbrook for reinforcements on the roster. When asked about that possibility following Jalen Williams' season-ending injury and Cason Wallace's shoulder surgery, Presti insisted he hadn't considered any roster moves at that time. 
"I haven't thought about anything relative to the roster spot," Presti said during a press conference last week. "I understand the question, but all I'm really focused on right now is players, getting them the right support, and then helping everybody with our group realize that, you know, we have a tremendous challenge in front of us."From a basketball perspective, the fit between Westbrook and this current Thunder roster would've perhaps been a bit clunky, but many wondered if OKC still might pursue it as a fitting, emotional send-off for the franchise's favorite son. With the announcement of his jersey retirement, that puts to rest any speculation he'll end his retirement to return to play for the Thunder. Still, he'll get to return to the only team he ever called home long-term -- and the only fan base that ever truly embraced him. "Let Westbrook be Westbrook" was a favorite saying during his prime years in Oklahoma City, and it's the only place he ever was able to do just that. After Kevin Durant left for the Warriors, Westbrook became the avatar of loyalty in OKC, and the Thunder faithful latched onto their star guard even more after feeling betrayed by Durant. 
While it didn't yield the championship Westbrook and Thunder fans hoped for during his tenure, he is the most beloved figure in franchise history for what he did to establish NBA basketball in Oklahoma City and give back to the community. On Feb. 7, he'll get a chance to receive a long-awaited warm welcome back to his adopted home and see the No. 0 get raised to the rafters.

title: Why Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg was benched after being 'peer pressured' into chasing 40 against Clippers - CBS Sports
description: Steve Kerr yanked Lendeborg with two minutes to play as the Clippers cut a 21-point lead to eight
body:
Steve Kerr yanked Lendeborg with two minutes to play as the Clippers cut a 21-point lead to eight
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has been a revelation to open his NBA career. Through his first seven games, he's putting up historic numbers, and he somehow keeps one-upping himself. On Sunday, he played his best game yet: 37 points on 85% true shooting. He made six of his 11 3-pointers and added six assists. He was outrageously good, as he has been all season, save for the Lakers game last Friday in which he was properly hazed by Luka Dončić. Other than that, it's been nothing but buckets for Lendeborg, who, given how easily all this has seemingly come for him, perhaps got a little ahead of himself by chasing the 40-point round number on Sunday with a couple of, shall we say, questionable shots at the end. Steve Kerr saw it, and with 2:14 to play, he benched his rookie as the Clippers were starting to make a desperate run, cutting a 21-point Warriors lead to eight over a two-minute span during which Lendeborg missed three 3-pointers, two of which were total chuck jobs. "He would've had 40 if we had just kept playing [normally]," Kerr said after the game. "The NBA game these days can change like that. We all know that. Almost every night, there's a 25-point lead that is overcome.
"The game changed when all the guys on the bench were yelling at Yax to get 40. He launched three kind of bad shots. A lesson is, if you just keep playing, then you stay in rhythm, you stay in flow, the ball moves, and then the game becomes much easier. I think that's the lesson for him and for our team. "But everybody loves Yax. Everybody wanted him to get 40. They were urging him to shoot from the bench, and It got us out of rhythm a little bit."As soon as Lendeborg went to the bench and the Warriors got back to business, De'Antony Melton, who was a stud all night, buried back-to-back 3s to put the game back on ice. It was a great night for the Warriors, who've won four straight after opening 0-3, and for Lendeborg, who continues to be a total open book who is more than willing to admit to his mistakes and vow not to repeat them, as he did after the Lakers debacle when he took full accountability for "wetting the bed." 
"I've never been a stat chaser in my life," Yaxel said after he was benched on Sunday. "So, I mean, just falling into peer pressure like I did just now was pretty much bad on my part. Especially just, I'm a guy that loves, like, ethical hoops. I'm a guy that loves efficient basketball, and I didn't do that for the last two to three minutes. So, it's kind of, like, bad on my part. Next time I definitely won't do that again. If it comes to me, it does. If I don't get it, then I wasn't meant to get it that day. So, I'm gonna be way better next time."Lendeborg elaborated on the peer pressure aspect of the chase, which, frankly, anyone can understand. You're a rookie and you're going off and your teammates are all cheering you on to keep shooting. The game, you think, is in the bag. Any player in that situation would've let a few more shots go. "De'Anthony Melton went up to me and said, 'Hey, man you need to get 40. You're three points away,'" Lendeborg said. "And I'm like, 'Nah, It's all good.' He just peer pressured me into doing it. ... He said he's gonna give me the ball, and he literally was holding it just to give me the ball. I'm like, all right, fine, I'll shoot it,' and I missed. I tried to tell him 'no, no, no,' and now Will [Richards] came over [to me saying], 'you gotta do it, you gotta do it.' 
"So everybody was just egging me on and I kind of just fell into it. But I know next time I'm just going to play in the flow of the game, because [the Clippers] came down and made like four threes in a row and we almost lost the game because of that. So next time I'm never doing that again."

title: Fantasy basketball Week 3 start/sit: Schedule strategy, best plays and risks - CBS Sports
description: Collin Gillespie and Jeremiah Fears offer strong upside across four-game schedules, while slumping options like M
body:
Collin Gillespie and Jeremiah Fears offer strong upside across four-game schedules, while slumping options like Mikal Bridges belong on the bench
        
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:37 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        Two weeks down, a lot of weeks remaining. Panic moves and overreactions are par for the course at this time of the year, meaning your sit/start decisions can be tricky. Week three will see 18 teams play four times, with the remaining 12 teams suiting up three times.Sitting players who only go three times has its advantages, but fantasy managers still have to make smart decisions when figuring out whom to play, regardless of game count. Being aware of back-to-back sets is also a key factor, especially with so many teams now sitting players due to injury management.Five Games: N/AFour Games: ATL, BKN, BOS, CLE, DAL, LAL, MIA, MIL, MIN, NOP, OKC, PHI, PHO, POR, SAC, SAS, UTA, WASThree Games: CHA, CHI, DEN, DET, GSW, HOU, IND, LAC, MEM, NYK, ORL, TORTwo Games: N/AHere are four potential starts and four potential sits entering the second week of the NBA season. Just keep in mind that this is based on games played for the week. If you play in a rotisserie league, the number of games played each week may not matter in your format.
GuardsConsider starting: Collin Gillespie, PHOOpponents: @GSW, POR, ORL, HOUGillespie is coming off easily his best game of the season, finishing with 16 points, 10 assists, four steals, three rebounds, one block and four three-pointers in 33.5 minutes during a loss to the Nuggets. While this was certainly a standout performance, the fact that Dillon Brooks was ejected definitely played a role, as did Jalen Green turning in another stinker. With that said, Gillespie playing more minutes on this team makes a lot of sense, especially with Green struggling to impact the game. His minutes are far from guaranteed, but given Phoenix has the best schedule of all the teams this week, starting Gillespie feels worth the risk.Consider starting: Jeremiah Fears, NOPOpponents: @MEM, UTA, MIN, @LACAfter a rough start to the season, Fears has turned things around in his past two games, averaging 21.0 points, 10.0 assists, 6.5 rebounds, 1.5 steals, 2.0 blocks and 2.0 three-pointers. Although these performances came while Dejounte Murray was sidelined due to personal reasons, they should do a lot in terms of building his confidence. He has started in all six games this season, so his role feels relatively secure. With four games coming up, rolling the dice on him to see if he can maintain his momentum, even with Murray likely returning, is a worthwhile gamble.Consider sitting: Jaylen Wells, MEMOpponents: NOP, IND, OKCMuch like Fears, Wells has been a regular starter for the Grizzlies. However, although his scoring has been serviceable, he offers very little else, which limits his overall appeal. Through six games, he has averaged 12.2 points, 1.2 steals and 1.8 three-pointers in 27.2 minutes per game. While the steals could be considered a positive, four of his seven came in the season-opener against Utah. With only three games coming up, it feels as though most managers should have a more versatile option on their roster this week.
ForwardsConsider starting: Miles Bridges, PHOOpponents: @GSW, POR, ORL, HOUQuietly, Bridges has started his career in Phoenix on a positive note, providing the team with serviceable production on both ends of the floor. In four games, he has averaged 16.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers and 1.8 combined steals and blocks, good enough for borderline top 50 value in standard category formats. Phoenix has lost three of its four games and is looking to find some answers. While Bridges is certainly not going to move the needle too much, he is doing more than enough to be inserted into starting lineups, given the favorable schedule this week.Consider sitting: Collin Murray-Boyles, TOROpponents: @LAC, @DEN, @MILDespite a decent amount of preseason hype, Murray-Boyles has been one of the most disappointing players so far this season, at least in relation to expectations. Through six appearances, he has been the 180th-ranked player in nine-category leagues, averaging 7.7 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.2 steals in 19.0 minutes per game. While the production has been very underwhelming, it's the lack of consistent playing time that raises more questions. During Sunday's loss to the Lakers and despite Jakob Poeltl being ruled out due to a shoulder concern, Murray-Boyles still only managed 20 minutes of playing time. The hope is that he will turn things around, but with only three games in the next seven days, now is a good time to move him to your bench.Consider sitting: Mikal Bridges, NYKOpponents: BKN, CHI, @CLESpeaking of disappointing starts to the season, let me introduce you to Mikal Bridges. In his six games thus far, he has averaged 6.2 points and 1.2 three-pointers in 27.4 minutes per contest, leaving him well outside the top 200 during that span. While his starting role doesn't seem to be in jeopardy, his poor end to the 2025-26 season has certainly carried over into the current campaign. Managers should be fine moving him to the bench this week, while dropping him altogether is certainly something to consider.
CentersConsider starting: Aday Mara, OKCOpponents: @CLE, CLE, @MEM, WASThere are still more questions than answers about Mara's role moving forward. Chet Holmgren is going to miss at least two months due to a knee injury, which firmly puts Mara on the standard league radar. A decent amount of hype during the preseason has probably filtered through to the season proper, meaning he is rostered in most leagues by now. If you have taken a chance on him, Saturday's loss to the Rockets was full of positives. He finished with seven points, nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks in 28 minutes. If that amount of playing time was a given, he would be a clear must-start player. However, he has now played at least 20 minutes in three straight games, averaging 8.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.7 blocks, shooting 52.9 percent from the field and 85.7 percent from the line. If you are open to a little risk, giving him a shot in your starting lineup feels pretty exciting.Consider sitting: Jalen Smith, CHIOpponents: @PHI, @NYK, PHIIt's been a strong start to the season for Smith, averaging 12.0 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers and 1.0 blocks in 24.1 minutes per game through six appearances. On the surface, it would make sense to at least consider him a starter-level player this week. However, it appears as though Nic Claxton could return from a hamstring injury sooner rather than later, which would almost certainly see Smith move back to the bench. Tiago Splitter has not been afraid to shuffle his rotation, with Smith's minutes ranging from 19 to 30 minutes. Given the varying risks, leaving him on the bench might be the safer option.

title: Oklahoma expected to promote Jason Witten to offensive coordinator after Ben Arbuckle firing - CBS Sports
description: The former Dallas Cowboys star makes a massive leap from the Texas private high school ranks to the SEC with vete
body:
The former Dallas Cowboys star makes a massive leap from the Texas private high school ranks to the SEC with veteran analyst Kevin Wilson expected to assist
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma is expected to elevate Jason Witten to offensive coordinator, sources confirmed to Sooners Illustrated. Witten joined the staff as tight ends coach in 2026. A future Hall of Fame tight end with the Dallas Cowboys, Witten moved to coaching after his final NFL season in 2020. He spent five years as head coach and offensive playcaller at Liberty Christian High School in Argyle, Texas. During his tenure, the program won its first two state championships in program history. Over a two-year stretch from 2023-24, Witten's Liberty Christian squad went a combined 26-1 and averaged 50.9 points per game. Quarterback Quinn Murphy, now at Baylor, threw for 3,152 yards, 40 touchdowns and five interceptions under Witten's tutelage. That said, Liberty Christian plays in TAPPS, the less-heralded private school version of Texas high school football. In Witten's final season, the Warriors went 1-2 against public school competition. 
Needless to say, the jump from private high school playcaller to the SEC is a significant one. According to reports, offensive analyst Kevin Wilson -- a former Sooners coordinator -- will play a supporting role. Oklahoma has three matchups remaining against AP Top 25 competition. Witten was a four-time All-Pro and 11-time Pro Bowler for the Dallas Cowboys as a tight end. He was named to the Texas Sports Hall of Fame in 2019. After his playing career, Witten received overtures to take on staff roles in the NFL and college football before opting to coach his son in high school.
Witten's son, Cooper, is a five-star linebacker in the Class of 2027. He plays at Liberty Christian and is committed to Oklahoma.

title: Baseball Hall of Fame: Contemporary Baseball Era Committee unveils 8 candidates - CBS Sports
description: The non-player ballot includes managers, executives, and umpires who did their most important work after 1980
body:
The non-player ballot includes managers, executives, and umpires who did their most important work after 1980
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The National Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown on Monday announced eight candidates for election on the 2027 Contemporary Baseball Era Committee ballot. The non-player ballot includes four former managers and four former executives: Sandy Alderson, Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, Joe Maddon, Lou Piniella, Brian Sabean, Ted Turner, and Bill White. The non-player ballot includes managers, executives, and umpires. On an alternating basis, the Era Committee also evaluates a ballot consisting of former players. As for the qualifications and criteria, the Hall of Fame describes it thus: "The eight Contemporary Baseball Era finalists were selected by the BBWAA-appointed Historical Overview Committee from all eligible candidates among managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980. Eligible candidates include managers and umpires with 10 or more major league seasons and retired for at least five years (candidates who are 65 years or older are eligible six months following retirement); and executives retired for at least five years (active executives 70 years or older are eligible for consideration regardless of the position they hold in an organization and regardless of whether their body of work has been completed). All candidates must not be on Baseball's Ineligible List."As for those figures on the Era Committee ballot for 2027, here's a quick rundown:Sandy AldersonAlderson built a powerhouse and won a World Series as general manager of the Oakland A's. He later earned multiple playoff berths and a pennant as GM of the New York Mets.Dusty BakerOne of the winningest managers of all time, Baker guided five different clubs to the playoffs and won three pennants and a World Series. His success in the dugout came after a long and distinguished playing career as an MLB outfielder. 
Bruce BochyBochy as a manager led three different clubs to the postseason and is one of just six managers ever to win at least four World Series. Three of Bochy's rings came with the San Francisco Giants, and the final one came with the Texas Rangers in 2023. Joe MaddonMaddon won more than 1,300 games as a manager for three different franchises. He also won a pennant as manager of the Tampa Bay Rays, and in 2016, he led the Chicago Cubs to their first World Series title in more than a century. Lou PiniellaAfter an 18-year playing career, Piniella racked up more than 1,800 wins as a big-league manager. He led three different clubs to the playoffs, won a World Series as manager of the 1990 Cincinnati Reds, and in 2001 helmed the Seattle Mariners to a record 116 wins during the regular season. 
Brian SabeanAfter filling a key role in the New York Yankees front office, Sabean joined the Giants as their general manager. Under his guidance, the Giants won the World Series in 2010, 2012, and 2014. Ted TurnerThe only posthumous candidate on the ballot, Turner owned the Atlanta Braves for two decades. Along the way, he innovated the distribution of televised baseball games and oversaw a dynasty. Under Turner's stewardship, the Braves claimed 14 straight division titles and won the World Series in 1995. Bill White A five-time All-Star and Gold Glove first baseman as a player, White after his playing days were over served as president of the National League. White was also the first Black play-by-play broadcaster in MLB history, and his leadership of the NL made him the first Black president of a major sports league.
The results of the committee vote will be announced on MLB Network at 8 p.m. ET on Sunday, Dec. 6. As with the BBWAA ballot, a candidate must be named on at least 75% of ballots in order to earn election. A 16-member committee will vote on the candidates.The more traditional BBWAA ballot, in which candidates are voted on by writers and other media members, will be revealed on Nov. 16. Results of the 2027 BBWAA ballot will be announced in January, at which point we'll know the full Hall of Fame class for 2027.

title: What's next for Mike Norvell? Potential paths for ex-FSU coach, including high-profile coordinator options - CBS Sports
description: Armed with a massive $50 million buyout, the former Seminoles coach could target an open head coaching role, rese
body:
Armed with a massive $50 million buyout, the former Seminoles coach could target an open head coaching role, reset as a coordinator or take a full year off
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mike Norvell is out of a job after Florida State fired him Sunday following a 36-24 loss to Clemson that dropped the Seminoles' record to 3-5.eFlorida State will owe Norvell nearly $50 million, subject to mitigation, in what is the third-largest buyout in college football history. Losing your job is never easy, though that substantial amount of money can afford Norvell the ability to be choosy in what he does next.There seem to be three main paths Norvell can take in 2027.Take another head coaching jobIt may not have worked out in the end, but Norvell has some strong resume points. He has four seasons of 10 or more wins (2 at Memphis, 2 at Florida State) and will always have that perfect 13-0 2023 regular season. Norvell has a reputation for a strong offensive mind and X's and O's expertise, too. Options for this cycle might be limited for Norvell, however. Unless the carousel really gets swinging and we see a significant domino effect, there just may not be that many Power Four and Group of Six jobs that feel like a fit. The most obvious would be a return to Memphis if Charles Huff gets a Power Four job elsewhere. Norvell has already had success at the school and knows it has the resources to do well at that level. 
North Carolina State is focused on Philip Rivers, which seemingly eliminates the Wolfpack as an option. It's still early in the Maryland and Baylor searches, though he could emerge as a possible candidate depending on the route those schools take. Last cycle we saw two fired coaches (Billy Napier, James Franklin) and one quasi-retired, quasi-pushed-out coach (Kyle Whittingham) quickly jump into new head coaching roles. This would be Norvell's preference, according to industry sources, but it'll need to be the right fit. Don't expect Norvell to pursue the vacant Sam Houston State job. Take an offensive coordinator jobIf there's not a viable, attractive head coaching opportunity, perhaps Norvell goes the offensive coordinator path. 
Oregon and Oklahoma, for instance, are in the market for new offensive coordinators after firing Drew Mehringer and Ben Arbuckle, respectively. Norvell and Oregon head coach Dan Lanning have a long-standing friendship, dating back to their days working on Todd Graham's Pittsburgh staff. They worked together at three different schools, including most recently at Memphis when Norvell hired Lanning as his inside linebackers coach. For both Oregon and Oklahoma, Norvell would be working for a defensive-minded head coach, which could be appealing and an easier transition as he moves from the big chair to an assistant role. In critical upcoming seasons for Lanning and Oklahoma coach Brent Venables, they need to nail the OC hire and could spend big to do so. There's not a financial incentive to work – Norvell could actually lose money having to pay state income taxes from a new job that would reduce FSU's buyout obligations – but it'd keep the fired coach in the mix. If he lands at the right program and has success, it could be easier to leapfrog into a new head coaching job than if he takes the year off. There's real value, even from just a public awareness standpoint, in reminding people what made you such a hot coaching candidate in the first place and not the one who got fired. 
Last coaching carousel, there were three coaches -- Neal Brown (North Texas), Blake Anderson (Southern Miss) and Will Hall (Tulane) -- who all got head coaching jobs as assistant coaches one year after being fired. Anderson and Hall seemed to especially pick the right landing spots, as each was an internal promotion to the head job after Huff left for Memphis and Jon Sumrall took the Florida job. Factoring in his previous success with FSU being on the hook for a massive buyout, Norvell would be a very attractive option for any school in the market for an offensive coordinator. Take a year offThis isn't Norvell's preference, but there can be value gained in getting a chance to reset, thoroughly understand what did and didn't work at Florida State and build a plan to succeed at the next job. That plan should include a well-thought-out coaching staff and personnel department after the struggles in his final seasons in Tallahassee. 
Norvell could visit friends at different schools and get a holistic sense of what is and isn't working in college football. Maybe he could even work as an unofficial consultant to keep his finger on the pulse and feel like he was still involved in the sport. The downside is it seems harder these days to jump from out of coaching directly into a head coaching opportunity. Pat Fitzgerald pulled it off last year with Michigan State, but his circumstances were unique. The previous cycle, Bill Belichick got the North Carolina job after spending an off-year working in various media capacities. His situation, too, was unique as the most successful coach in NFL history. Elsewhere, former Texas A&M coach Jimbo Fisher has been out of coaching since 2023 and hasn't gotten much traction in searches. He is expected to be a candidate for the Florida State job but didn't have any luck in last year's very busy cycle. Neither did Ed Orgeron, who had expressed public interest in the Oregon State job that ultimately went to JaMarcus Sheppard. Orgeron is now on Lane Kiffin's LSU staff. 
Former Notre Dame and LSU coach Brian Kelly, now working as a CBS Sports analyst, could be a good barometer this cycle. The longer a coach is out of the space, the harder it seems to be to get back in. There are exceptions, however, including former Nebraska coach Scott Frost, who took a year off and then spent a season with the Los Angeles Rams before returning to UCF as head coach.

title: Oklahoma expected to fire Ben Arbuckle: Sooners to part with OC as offense continues to sputter in 2026 season - CBS Sports
description: The Sooners are moving on from their second-year offensive coordinator after an embarrassing loss to South Caroli
body:
The Sooners are moving on from their second-year offensive coordinator after an embarrassing loss to South Carolina left Oklahoma at No. 15 in the SEC in total offense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma is expected to fire offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle in his second season, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The Sooners suffered a brutal 42-25 loss to South Carolina on Saturday at home, where Oklahoma was held to three first-half points on offense. Arbuckle, 31, was an innovative hire coming from Washington State, where he helped lead one of the most explosive offenses in college football. He was hired by Oklahoma in 2024 and brought along starting quarterback John Mateer, the No. 3 quarterback in the transfer portal that year. After an inconsistent first season marred by a hand injury to Mateer, Oklahoma's offense has tanked in Year 2. The Sooners rank No. 15 in the SEC in both total and scoring offense, despite getting multiple scores on defense and special teams. Arbuckle's firing continues a revolving door of offensive staff changes under coach Brent Venables, whose production has fallen off dramatically since Jeff Lebby left for Mississippi State. Venables fired Seth Littrell after seven games into his first season in 2024, and also fired multiple assistant coaches after the 2025 season. 
The Sooners are careening towards their third losing season in five years under Venables, and are at serious risk of missing their first bowl game since John Blake's final season in 1998. Oklahoma sits at 4-4 with No. 12 Ole Miss, No. 19 Missouri and No. 25 Florida coming in the weeks ahead. Mateer's woesThe transfer quarterback Mateer was billed as a potential game-changing addition after Oklahoma's quarterback issues in 2024. The Sooners limped through the season with five-star starter Jackson Arnold and true freshman Michael Hawkins Jr., both of whom transferred out of the program. There were flashes early in Mateer's career, including throwing for 270 yards, rushing for 74 yards and scoring three total touchdowns against No. 15 Michigan in 2025. But since his hand surgery a year ago, Mateer has been miserable. 
Mateer finished with 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions last season. He's at 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this year, though his rushing has been limited to 1.7 yards per carry. In a 21-13 loss to Kentucky, Mateer threw one touchdown and three interceptions. Oklahoma believed it was only a quarterback away, but making a change has only led to more miserable results. Issues go deeperArbuckle struggled to remake the Oklahoma offense in his image, but the issues go far deeper than playcalling. The Sooners have been a horrendous offensive line operation for most of the past five years, and the consequences have only gotten worse 
The Sooners rank No. 131 in the country at 3.2 yards per carry, and have scored a nation-worst three rushing touchdowns. Oklahoma is rated the No. 105 run-blocking unit in the country per Pro Football Focus, behind UTEP. Oklahoma missed top offensive lineman Michael Fasusi for several games, but the unit has been disastrous regardless. After the season, Venables will have no choice but to evaluate longtime offensive line coach Bill Bedenbaugh. No offensive coordinator will have success with the inconsistency up front. Where do they turn?Assuming Venables is back in 2027, Oklahoma's offensive coordinator search will be complicated. The new hire will be the Sooners' sixth new playcalling staff in six years, with the last two full-time hires each fired midseason after fewer than two years in the job. Coaching offense under Venables since Lebby left -- and former coach Lincoln Riley's players matriculated out of the program -- has been a dead-end job. 
After whiffing on a young up-and-comer, there will likely be pressure on Venables to hire an established coach. Venables continues to call the defense, and the offense has atrophied during the process. With a head coach only committed on one side of the ball, Oklahoma could take a page out of Texas's book and hire a "head coach of the offense" type role. The question is, how attractive is coaching for the short-tempered Venables while he's firmly on the hot seat? Could Oklahoma convince Mike Norvell to take the job, or will it be trying to attract a second-tier candidate?

title: Should Ravens trade for QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries? Possible candidates to watch - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore could be without Jackson for the rest of the year
body:
Baltimore could be without Jackson for the rest of the year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Ravens' quarterback situation went from disappointing to dire to destitute in a hurry Sunday. In his return from an ankle injury that cost him three games, Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will require potentially season-ending surgery on Baltimore's first offensive play, and backup Tyler Huntley left shortly thereafter with a toe injury.That left the Ravens with emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie. He went 10-for-21 for 91 yards and an interception, looking very much like an undrafted rookie, as the Ravens went down quietly, 36-10, against the Bills. What looked like a chance to turn the season around now looks like a game that could end Baltimore's season, for all intents and purposes. The Ravens are 4-4 and have lost three straight. Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Huntley will miss extended time with turf toe, a bothersome injury that can last for weeks.The Ravens have little time to wallow. They play the Jaguars on Thursday night. Currently, Baltimore has one available quarterback on its active roster (Fagnano), and even he was in discomfort late after taking several big hits. The Ravens don't have another quarterback on their active roster or practice squad; Skylar Thompson is on IR.So where does Baltimore go from here at the position? There are many factors to consider.
Why the Ravens should trade for a quarterbackRegardless of whether the Ravens can continue to contend or not — and it's very much looking like the latter — they owe it to all parties involved to get a quarterback.They owe it to the rest of the team, which is still fighting. Baltimore is 4-4, which isn't good, but isn't completely out of it. It's not as if the team is dead in the water, just trying to finish out a completely lost season. There's still Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers on offense and plenty of stars on defense. If there's any hope Jackson can return on the sooner end of the recovery spectrum, Baltimore's players deserve a chance to keep their season afloat.They owe it to coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, the latter of whom has been excellent this year. Forcing Minter, a first-year head coach, to resort to an undrafted rookie free agent would be extremely difficult. Since 2000, only one team with a rookie head coach has started an undrafted rookie quarterback in multiple games: the Jets with Brady Cook last year. The Ravens do not want to resemble the Jets whatsoever. 
They owe it to Fagnano, too. He is a really nice story, someone who started his college career as a walk-on at FCS program Maine and finished it with a superb seventh-year senior season at UConn. He earned a spot on the roster with a stellar showing at rookie tryouts, then throughout the early offseason, and then in training camp and the preseason. But to stick him with an extended starting role would be unfair to him, just as it would be for Minter and Doyle.And the bottom line is the Ravens have to add someone. They can't have one quarterback on the active roster. Austin Reed makes sense as a temporary solution to join Fagnano, as he was at least with the team this offseason, but he has never taken an NFL snap.Unfortunately, it's not like capable quarterbacks grow on trees. There's a shortage of passable starting quarterbacks, much less backups or backups to backups. But that doesn't mean it would be impossible to find one.
Rumored trade targetsRapoport said he'd expect the Ravens to consider quarterback trades. Two names he floated were Bears backup Tyson Bagent and Cardinals recently benched starter Jacoby Brissett.
Bagent, 26, makes sense for a few reasons. First and foremost, he was with Doyle in Chicago last year. Second, it's unclear whether he's even Caleb Williams' primary backup right now. He performed decently in a win over the Jets earlier this year but struggled badly in a loss to the Packers the following week. Overall, he has zero passing touchdowns and three interceptions in three games (two starts) this year. Case Keenum, on the other hand, played well in his lone start, a win over the Eagles. He got the nod after Bagent had missed much of the week of practice with a concussion, though Bagent returned to primary backup thereafter.
The Bears clearly value Bagent. They gave him a multi-year extension last season. He has shown promise in extremely small sample sizes. He has some creation ability and athleticism, which are helpful in Doyle's offense. All of that also means he wouldn't be cheap, either. There's little reason for Chicago, in a win-now season, to part with Bagent. What if the Bears need a spot start from a backup late in the year? Maybe Baltimore could sweeten the deal by sending a depth piece of their own to Chicago in the deal.The Ravens must determine how much they want to invest in saving the next few weeks. Bagent would be on the pricier end, and it's not as if his performance this season has inspired much confidence. If Baltimore believes he could eke out a couple of wins, though? Maybe it's worth it.
Brissett has been the Cardinals' de facto bridge starter this year, but he may have lost that position Sunday, when he was benched. In his place, Gardner Minshew threw for three touchdowns in Arizona's stunning 33-30 overtime comeback win over the Cowboys. Mike LaFleur did not commit to Minshew being the starter going forward, but it'd be hard to imagine he's not.
That will be especially true if the Ravens come knocking regarding Brissett. Over the past two seasons, out of 30 quarterbacks, Brissett ranks ...28th in net yards per attempt24th in EPA per dropback22nd in touchdown-to-interception ratioHe is exactly what he has been during his entire career: a low-level starter or high-level backup who has gotten an opportunity to be the starter only when the need arises.But the need is there for Baltimore, and perhaps Arizona feels the opposite. Minshew is pretty similar in terms of overall player archetype, and the Cardinals also have rookie Carson Beck. If Arizona feels OK with Minshew and Beck, and it can get a solid draft-capital return for Brissett, it could make sense to do so, especially at this point in the Cardinals' long-term timeline.
Other options?There are some other names that could be considered, though Bagent and Brissett stand out as more natural/sensical picks. If Baltimore goes elsewhere, though, here are a few names worth mentioning. View this as throwing names at a wall and seeing what sticks.Anthony Richardson Jr. requested a trade from the Colts earlier this year. He hasn't gotten one, but the Colts are blowing it up this trade deadline, and even a late-round pick swap could be attractive for Indianapolis. A Richardson-Henry backfield certainly carries a lot of downhill running heft.Spencer Rattler did some good things (and some not-so-good things) as a starter for the Saints before Tyler Shough took over in the Big Easy.Jalen Milroe and Joe Milton are two other mobile quarterbacks buried on depth charts. Milroe seems less likely to move — the Seahawks could want to develop him as a potential successor to Drew Lock as Sam Darnold's backup — but Milton has always been a mystery wrapped in an enigma. He has a rocket arm, legit mobility and wild athleticism. He'd be frustrating at many times but potentially fun at others.There are always practice squad options such as old friend Josh Johnson. A move on this level could be possible just to have a second available quarterback this week.Why to not expect Mac JonesIn the coming days, you'll likely hear Mac Jones' name bandied about in connection to Baltimore.It doesn't seem particularly realistic. Kyle Shanahan has said many times he wants to keep Jones, and the 49ers, like the Bears, have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations right here, right now. If the 49ers needed a spot start — or even just a few series — from Jones to win a game, it would be worth it. Unlike the Bears, though, the 49ers don't have a second legit backup. Kurtis Rourke has never played an NFL snap.
The Ravens would likely need to blow away the 49ers to have any shot at Jones, and that simply hasn't been Baltimore GM Eric DeCosta's M.O. Instead, Bagent and Brissett seem like top options, with a flyer on a younger, potentially intriguing player also a legitimate route for the Ravens to take.

title: Grading every NBA lottery pick's first two weeks as impressive 2026 rookie class dazzles early - CBS Sports
description: Darius Acuff Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson are just some of the names who have looked gre
body:
Darius Acuff Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer and Caleb Wilson are just some of the names who have looked great so far
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If there's one takeaway from the first two weeks of the 2026-27 NBA season (other than the fact that there are way too many injuries), it might be this: this rookie class has the potential to be the best in league history. Maybe that's an overreaction and a case of recency bias, but the stats and film don't lie.This group of players was heralded as one of the best freshmen classes in college basketball history. Not only did those players meet expectations, but they also went beyond them. It's hard to see a collection of talent hitting college basketball again like that for a long time.Wizards forward AJ Dybantsa was late to the party, but the No. 1 overall pick finally made his debut last week against the Cavaliers after missing the first four games due to an ankle injury. Dybantsa scored 19 points in his first game while being on a minutes restriction.The biggest surprise in the NBA is the Memphis Grizzlies, the only team in the association that hasn't suffered a loss. Cameron Boozer, who has seemingly won at every place he's played — whether in high school, Team USA, Duke and now the NBA — remains the favorite to win NBA Rookie of the Year over Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. and Bulls forward Caleb Wilson.
With the first two weeks of the season in the books, it's time to assess the play of every lottery pick from the 2026 NBA Draft by handing out some early grades. Let's dive in, starting with Dybantsa.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    AJ Dybantsa, Wizards: A-
It took exactly 16 seconds to showcase one of Dybantsa's elite skills: drawing contact at the rim. In 35 games last season at BYU, Dybantsa attempted 296 free throws, which ranked No. 1 among all college players. That's going to be a huge part of his game throughout his career because of how good he is at getting into the lane and drawing fouls. He has already attempted nine free throws in his first two games. Dybantsa is still on a minutes restriction. 
Once that restriction gets lifted, he will play even more than the 57 minutes he played during the first two games combined. The Wizards have a chance to be a sleeper play-in team in a loaded Eastern Conference this season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Darryn Peterson, Utah Jazz: B
Peterson's role with Utah is still being established. Something that stood out to me was Jazz coach Will Hardy benching Peterson for the final stretch against the Spurs last week, even though the game went to overtime and the team was already without Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. There were a handful of plays in the fourth quarter where Peterson didn't make the right read on the defensive end, but the decision to bench the young rookie and only play him 26 minutes might've cost Utah a chance to steal a game at home. Despite Peterson still trying to find a clear-cut role, he ranks fifth in his rookie class among field goals attempted (78) this season. Peterson thrives on-ball but is also very capable off the ball. That's why I really liked him as a fit with the Jazz. Peterson is going to figure it out. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cameron Boozer, Memphis Grizzlies: A
Boozer is the ultimate winner. Since high school, Boozer has a 155-17 record across games in high school, at Duke and in the NBA. It should come as no surprise that he's contributing to winning at the highest level. Boozer had his first career triple-double (18/12/12) and followed it up with a career-high 27 points against Sacramento. Even when Boozer isn't playing well, he can still impact winning with his passing. 
He is an elite processor of the game and it's only going to get better throughout his career. The one concern I do have about Boozer is the rim finishing. Per Synergy, he is shooting 42.4% at the rim. Aside from that, Boozer has been awesome. If the Grizzlies keep winning, Boozer should be the favorite to win Rookie of the Year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Caleb Wilson, Chicago Bulls: A
The Bulls are off to a slow start, but Wilson is not. The way he can impact both ends of the floor remains one of his strengths. Wilson is also fearless and won't back down from anybody. Two of my favorite plays so far from the NBA season came in Bulls vs. Celtics games. On the defensive end, Wilson recovered while Jayson Tatum was driving middle and rejected him at the rim with his off hand. In a game against Boston days before, Wilson had the ball at the top of the key against Paul George, jab-stepped left and dunked it while taking contact. 
He is averaging 3.2 stocks (steals and blocks) per game. Another note: He is taking 7.8 (!) 3-pointers per game after taking 27 total attempts at North Carolina last season. The efficiency (29.8%) isn't there yet, but if Wilson's shooting ticks up, it changes his entire ceiling.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Keaton Wagler, Los Angeles Clippers: B+
Wagler has been playing in a sixth man role during the first two weeks. The Clippers are trying to bring him along slowly. I'll say this: It's time to start Wagler. He has looked very comfortable even dating back to his first minutes against Sacramento. Wagler is shooting better from 3 (31.3%) than 2 (24%), but I'm not super worried about the efficiency for him or any rookie guard on the list for one reason: Rookie guards are historically inefficient. Again, it's understandable why the Clippers want to wait to start Wagler, but it's time to put him in the starting lineup and play him even more. Wagler has shown he's capable of taking on that responsibility while running the second unit.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mikel Brown Jr., Brooklyn Nets: B
Similar to Wagler, Brown is coming off the bench to begin his career. He has played over 25 minutes just once this season due to the team placing him on a minutes restriction. Brown also didn't play against Indiana last weekend due to back injury management. In the game (against Boston), where Brown played over 25 minutes, he was electric in the fourth quarter. Brown scored 13 of his 17 points in the final frame, including a corner 3-pointer to send the game to overtime. Brown made a rookie mistake in overtime, attempting a layup with less than five seconds remaining, with his team up by one and the shot clock off. 
After that miss, Tatum knocked down a game-winner. Brown had NBA range during his time at Louisville, and that was on display against the Celtics. It's just a matter of time before Brooklyn lifts the minutes restriction and throws him into the starting lineup.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Darius Acuff Jr., Sacramento Kings: A
Acuff has become the most polarizing rookie to talk about. The Kings are bad. Like, potentially the worst team in the league. However, Acuff has been the bright spot. His shotmaking is second-to-none in his class. When Acuff is hot, he can score at will. Acuff joined exclusive company earlier this week when he finished with 34 points and 14 assists against the Pelicans. The only other teenager in NBA history to post at least 30 points and 12 assists in a game, per CBS Sports research? LeBron James. 
Acuff has the ultimate green light in Sacramento. It's going to stay that way throughout his rookie season. It feels more like a matter of when, not if, Acuff scores 45+ points in a game. It might even come before the calendar flips to 2027

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kingston Flemings, Atlanta Hawks: B
Flemings' best game came last week against Miami, when he finished with 23 points, five assists, five rebounds and a block/steal. Flemings' role with the Hawks this season was always going to be off the bench, so it shouldn't come as a surprise that he has scored 27 points combined in the other six games he has played in. Flemings doesn't have to score to make an impact on the game. He was heralded as one of the best two-way players in the class, which was on display in his last game against New Orlenos when he recorded four steals. Flemings uses his speed to his advantage to get to the rim, create his own shot and change the pace. Despite taking six field goal attempts per game, Flemings has been very efficient (47.6%). 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Morez Johnson Jr., Dallas Mavericks: B-
Johnson has come off the bench in his first six games under his former college coach, Dusty May. Although his numbers don't necessarily pop, Johnson is going to be a very impactful player, especially on the defensive end of the floor. He's capable of guarding 1-5, which is super valuable when/if the Mavs decide to switch everything on defense.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brayden Burries, Milwaukee Bucks: BBurries is coming off the bench for the Bucks, which somewhat surprises me. He was awesome in summer league and should be playing more than 16 minutes per game. 
Burries did have one of the highlights of the season so far with a poster dunk over Tristan Enaruna. That game was also the highest-scoring (14 points) game of his so far.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Yaxel Lendeborg, Golden State Warriors: A+
Lendeborg is one of the most entertaining players to watch. You either love him or hate him, but you're still going to watch. It should come as no surprise that it took him exactly one game to talk trash to the opponent, which nearly backfired when Luka Dončić went on to drop 37 points less than 10 days after the season opener. 
The highs of Lendeborg's rookie season so far have been fantastic. Even though he had his worst statistical game against the Lakers, he finished with at least 25 points in three consecutive games, including a 31-point, 12-rebound outburst against the Nuggets. Yes, Lendeborg may be the oldest rookie from the first round of the draft, but it's clear to see why the Warriors drafted him. He is already Golden State's second-best player behind Steph Curry, which shouldn't even be that hot of a take. Lendeborg was awesome in a win over the Clippers and scored a career-high 37 points. He should be the co-favorite with Boozer for ROTY. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Aday Mara, Oklahoma City Thunder: B+
It's going to be sink-or-swim for Mara, with Chet Holmgren becoming the latest Thunder player to suffer an injury that will sideline him for multiple weeks. Mara logged 28 minutes against the Rockets and finished with seven points, nine rebounds and four blocks. Mara was one of the most efficient scorers at the rim and also one of the top shot blockers in college basketball because of his long 7-foot-3 frame. Mara has a chance to contribute in a larger role with Holmgren out. He's going to be just fine. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Nate Ament, Milwaukee Bucks: B
Ament was a DNP-CD in Ament's first two games before making his first appearance against the 76ers. Ament has skill and potential but is one of the rawest players drafted in the lottery. The Bucks are bringing him on slowly, which should do wonders for his development. He shot under 40% from the field last season at Tennessee but has been solid in that department (45.8% from the field, 44.4% from 3) in four games. The sample size isn't large enough to give a definitive grade, but Ament has shown signs of improvement since his college days. He has also been solid on the defensive end of the floor. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Hannes Steinbach, Charlotte Hornets: INC
Steinbach has played in just two games this season, both of which came in garbage time. He played 12 minutes in a 121-81 loss to the Hawks and two minutes against the Wizards last week. Coming into the season, I expected Steinbach to play a larger role. That could still happen later in the season, but the sample size so far isn't large enough to hand out a letter grade.

title: Fantasy Football Week 9 risers and fallers: Jonah Coleman takes over in Denver - CBS Sports
description: Jonah Coleman takes control of Denver's backfield, while Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers face uncertainty in Baltim
body:
Jonah Coleman takes control of Denver's backfield, while Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers face uncertainty in Baltimore
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In theory, we shouldn't be as desperate in Week 9 as we have been the past few weeks. Only two teams are on a bye: the Steelers and the Titans. We're getting a lot more good Fantasy starters back off of bye than we're losing. So yeah, Week 9 should be easier. Just don't tell that to anyone who has Ravens on their roster. They lost their top two quarterbacks and are on a short week at Jacksonville. It's a nightmare situation, but as you will see in the fallers section below, it may not mean that you're benching Zay Flowers or Derrick Henry. Prominent players we projected last week that we are not projecting to play in Week 8 as of Monday evening: Lamar Jackson, Jeremiyah Love, Zonovan Knight, Kendrick Bourne, Hunter Henry, Jake FergusonAt the bottom of this article are my Week 9 projections for quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and tight end. They will be updated throughout the week as we get more information.
 Risers Jared Goff, QB, Lions
This one is pretty simple. Goff faced the Vikings last week. He faces the Dolphins this week. They have given up the fifth-most Fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite the fact that they have seen the second-fewest pass attempts. There is some risk that Jahmyr Gibbs scores all the touchdowns, but the bottom line is that you should start all of your Lions this week.Patrick Mahomes, QB, Chiefs
Mahomes faced the Seahawks and the Broncos the last two weeks. Now he gets the Jets. Like Goff, there is a little risk that the run game is too dominant and Mahomes doesn't throw enough passes. But efficiency-wise, Mahomes is having his best season since 2022 and Rashee Rice looks to be 100% healthy. Mahomes isn't quite a must-start like Goff is, but he is back inside the top 10 QBs for this week.Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos
We thought the takeover might happen eventually. We did not expect it to be this immediate. Coleman was the clear lead back in Week 8, with a 67.9% snap share, a 47.8% rush share, and a 17.2% target share. Coleman is averaging nearly a yard more per carry than the other Broncos and this week gets a plus matchup against the Panthers. Coleman is easily a top 20 running back and I wouldn't be surprised if he is top 15 by the end of the week. Just hope the Broncos aren't one of the teams trying to trade for a running back. It doesn't look like they need to.
Tyler Allgeier, RB, Cardinals
This one is tricky. On the one hand, Jeremiyah Love and Zonovan Knight left Week 8 with injuries. And Allgeier was awesome after they left. On the other hand, Allgeier is facing the Seattle Seahawks. As of Monday evening, he projects for 19 touches and 12.7 PPR Fantasy points, which makes him a top 20 back, but he could fall closer to RB25 by the end of the week. At the very least, he should be one of the top waiver wire priorities, as he's only rostered in 45% of leagues.Jameson Williams, WR, Lions
Part of Williams' rise is the same as Jared Goff's. He's playing the Dolphins. They have actually been a bad matchup for receivers because of the volume, but they give up huge plays regularly, which is Williams' specialty. Maybe more importantly, he has a 26.8% target share in the two games since the Lions bye. It was during the bye week last year that Dan Campbell insisted Williams be more involved in the offense, and it looks like it may have happened again.Eli Raridon, TE, Patriots
Hunter Henry left Week 8 with a foot injury, and as of Monday night, we aren't expecting him to play in Week 9. That should open the door for the Patriots' rookie tight end to be their full-time TE1, and he has a ton of upside. He's averaged 8.65 yards per target so far this season and should see a target share near 20% if Henry is out. If A.J. Brown misses another game as well, then Raridon may just be Drake Maye's number one option against Green Bay. 
FallersGeno Smith, QB, Jets
Smith was our top streaming option last week against the Raiders, and he paid off with 22 Fantasy points. Unfortunately, now he's headed to Arrowhead to face a very good Chiefs defense coming off a loss to the Broncos. He is not in the streaming conversation this week. That being said, he does get the Bills in Week 10, so if you have room to stash him and a Week 10 need, he is worth holding on to. Derrick Henry, RB, Ravens
Henry has had 60 or fewer yards from scrimmage in each of his last three games. He has one touchdown in that stretch. Now he'll face arguably the best run defense in the NFL on Thursday night. In the projections, he's still a top-20 running back but if the Ravens don't make an emergency move to find a QB, I am not sure I can rank him in the top 24. Try to find someone else to start. Henry has always been better in wins than losses and at this point I don't know how many wins the Ravens have left on the schedule.Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders
Jeanty had two rush attempts in Week 8. Two. Mike Washington Jr. had 25. It's astonishing, and I am not sure that split holds, but Jeanty is an obvious faller. You may be surprised to see that he is still a top 20 back in full PPR. That's because he is still the pass-catching back and he is very good in that role. The Raiders are more than a touchdown underdog this week against the 49ers, so they should be throwing a lot, which will prop Jeanty up in that format. In non-PPR, I don't want to start either of the Raiders running backs in this game script.
Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens
Woof. Flowers scored zero Fantasy points last week and will likely be playing with a third-string quarterback. Much like Henry, Flowers didn't fall as far in the initial rankings as I projected. I would assume they will find ways to get him the ball against a Jacksonville defense that has struggled against the pass, but I also plan to rank Flowers considerably lower than his projection implies. He's probably in the Tre Tucker part of the rankings, because both could make your day with one play, but both have almost zero floor.Kyle Pitts, TE, Falcons
I hope it was just the rain, but Michael Penix was an absolute disaster in Week 8. Pitts' efficiency for the season is flat-out bad; his 6.2 yards per target would be the second-lowest mark of his career, and he's only averaging four targets per game. I do not want to start him this week against a Broncos defense that could overwhelm Penix. I would strongly prefer Raridon if Henry is out.Week 9 quarterback projections Week 9 running back projections  Week 9 wide receiver projections  Week 9 tight end projections

title: Is Jadarian Price playing against the Bears? Latest Seahawks RB injury update for 'Monday Night Football' - CBS Sports
description: The Seahawks could activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve before Monday night's g
body:
The Seahawks could activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve before Monday night's game, but Mike Macdonald offered few clues about the rookie's status
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:31 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Imagn Images
            
            

    
        Week 8 concludes on Monday night in Seattle, as the Seahawks (4-3) host the Chicago Bears (5-2) at Lumen Field. Running back Zach Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in Seattle's NFC divisional round playoff win against the San Francisco 49ers in January, is primed to make his 2026 season debut. He doesn't have a game status on Seattle's final injury report, indicating he will be available to play. The situation for First-round rookie running back Jadarian Price is slightly murkier.Why the lack of clarity with Price's situation? That is because Price, who has missed the last four games with a chest injury while on injured reserve, would need to be activated by 4 p.m. today. Seattle, however, has already designated Price to return with ESPN among those reporting he will play."We're going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one," coach Mike Macdonald said. 
If the defending Super Bowl champions are going to defeat the high-flying Bears attack led by quarterback Caleb Williams, the Seahawks will need to run the football. Doing so will not only keep Williams on the sideline but also slow down Chicago's pass rush. That second part is key for Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold since he has the NFL's worst expected points added (EPA) per dropback when pressured at -0.63. That's why Seattle traded for Quenton Nelson, and there's a likely chance Nelson will be able to block for both of the Seahawks' top backs in his Seattle debut."We have a plan for Zach and with JD," Macdonald said on Saturday. "If we were to make a move, that would happen on Monday to my knowledge. We'll see if that's what we do. We have some things going on roster-wise that we're working through right now, but we have a plan for Zach."
The Seahawks don't have to activate Price on Monday, but they have two more weeks to make a decision on his status before he would be required to move to season-ending injured reserve. On the off chance Price isn't activated for Week 8, Charbonnet would likely share the rushing workload with Emanuel Wilson. Wilson leads the Seahawks in rushing yards (403), rushing touchdowns (three) and carries (111) .

body:
Three of the best (and youngest) players in college basketball this season won't be eligible for the 2027 NBA Draft and will play two seasons of college hoops. Here's why
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Three players expected to be among the best in college basketball during the 2026-27 season will have to wait longer than usual to enter the NBA Draft. In a world of one-and-done freshmen, Duke's Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje, UCLA's Nikola Kusturica and Texas' Marcus Spears Jr. --- three expected stars this college basketball season --- are in a rare situation: All three must play at least two seasons of college basketball before entering the NBA Draft because of the league's age requirement.Why can't they enter the upcoming 2027 NBA Draft?NBA rules state that a player must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft.Spears doesn't turn 18 until April 18, 2027Kusturica doesn't turn 18 until April 30, 2027Boumtje Boumtje, the youngest of the group, doesn't turn 18 until May 30, 2027Because of this rule, Boumtje Boumtje, Kusturica and Spears will not be eligible for the 2027 NBA draft and must wait until the 2028 draft to enter the league. What makes this situation even more special is that all three have a chance to be really good players in Year 1 and then headline the sport in Year 2.This not only provides roster stability with incredible talents for Duke, UCLA, and Texas, but also gives college basketball fans a few household names for more than one year.
If Boumtje Boumtje, Kusturica and Spears were eligible for the 2027 NBA Draft, they would compete to go No. 1 overall this summer.Entering the season, Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes is the projected No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NBA Draft.While the race for the top pick is expected to be competitive like last season's draft that saw AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer compete to go No. 1, this year's class doesn't project to have the true star power like that class did top to bottom. In short: even though the lottery system has changed to the 3-2-1 format, all eyes will be on 2028 when Boumtje Boumtje, Spears and Kusturica are eligible.

        
            
                Final Four expert picks: Who will win the 2027 NCAA Tournament and more bold predictions for this season
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The most recent example? Look no further than Jayden Quaintance in the 2026 draftTypically, when a player reclassifies to play college basketball a year early, it's to be eligible for the draft the following year. That wasn't the case when former Arizona State and Kentucky big man Jayden Quaintance reclassified up to the 2024 class to play college basketball a year early. Quaintance averaged 9.4 points, 7.9 rebounds and 2.6 blocks during his freshman 2024-25 season at ASU as the youngest player in Division I basketball. Quaintance had surgery on a torn ACL after the season ended and then transferred to Kentucky, where he entered the season as a potential top-10 pick.However, after playing just four games at Kentucky due to injury, his draft stock took a hit. Still, Quaintance was selected 20th overall by the Spurs despite missing almost the entire season with the Wildcats. Quaintance underwent another knee surgery after the draft, and a timeline to make his NBA debut remains unclear.
Quaintance was one of the most unique transfer portal entrants ever, given his situation. Still, he probably wasn't as good of a prospect as Boumtje Boumtje, who already looks like one of the best two-way players in the sport despite being 17 years old.
        
            
                2026-27 college basketball predictions: National title odds, conference winners, sleeper picks
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Marcus Spears Jr. was the latest player to reclassifySpears was ranked as the No. 1 player in the 2027 recruiting class before reclassifying up to the 2026 class and publicly committing to Texas on July 9 (he actually enrolled at Texas days earlier on June 30). He finished as the No. 8 player in the 2026 class. The addition of Spears solidified Texas as one of the biggest winners of the offseason after the Longhorns and Coach Sean Miller landed David Punch and Isaiah Johnson from the transfer portal and signed six high school players, including five-star guard Austin Goosby.
Earlier this month, Coach Miller said it would be "too early to tell" if Spears would begin the season as a starter.Spears' development might take more time, especially if he comes off the bench to begin the season. According to CBS Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finkelstein, Spears is a 6-foot-9 wing lefty forward loaded with versatile long-term tools. He's mobile, runs the floor well, and has effortless athleticism. While he's a bouncy finisher around the rim, he also has budding skill with soft natural hands, touch, and developing floor-spacing potential as a shooter. Regardless of whether he starts or not, Spears is expected to be a key rotation player for the No. 7 Longhorns this season.

        
            
                College basketball conference power rankings: Massive spending helps SEC reclaim top spot entering 2026-27
                
                    David Cobb                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Boumtje Boumtje and Kusturica waited late in the cycle to signBoumtje Boumtje was the first domino to fall earlier this spring when he committed to Duke. Months later, Kusturica signed with UCLA to give the program its best NBA Draft prospect since the Bruins landed Lonzo Ball nearly a decade ago. Both players are considered two of the most prized international prospects in years.Despite Boumtje Boumtje playing for FC Barcelona the last two seasons, he grew up in the United States before moving to Spain at 14. This summer, Boumtje Boumtje scored 20 points and grabbed 15 rebounds in a 107–81 win over Kusturcia's Serbia squad in the FIBA U17 World Cup final.Kusturcia scored a tournament-record 37 points in that game against Team USA, but it wasn't enough. He committed to UCLA days after that game, picking the Bruins over Kentucky and Michigan. Boumtje Boumtje and Kusturcia were once teammates at FC Barcelona and could've stayed in Spain another season before coming to the States to play college basketball. However, they decided to enroll in college a year early to face better competition in the United States and make more money before entering the NBA.

        
            
                Meet Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje: Duke's 7-foot phenom and next potential No. 1 draft pick
                
                    Eric Bossi                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Boumtje Boumtje has gotten significant buzz due to his play in Duke's exhibition opener against Belmont. He finished with a team-high 19 points in 22 minutes and shot 7-of-11 from the field during the Blue Devils' 102-62 win. Boumtje Boumtje is expected to start at the four this season next to veteran center Patrick Ngongba II.Kusturcia is also projected to start for UCLA. The Bruins have a marquee season-opener against No. 5 Arizona in Las Vegas that will feature a matchup of two of the best first-year players in the sport: Kusturcia and five-star freshman Caleb Holt. Kusturcia showcased his versatility on both ends of the floor during UCLA's exhibition games when he finished with 10 points, eight rebounds, six assists, five steals, two blocks and zero turnovers in 24 minutes against Cal Baptist.This exact scenario playing out this season could become a trend, driven by five-for-five and the international market in college basketball becoming more robust than ever. Kusturcia, Spears and Boumtje Boumtje are set to be three of the biggest stars in the sport this season. 
The best news of all? College basketball fans will get them for two seasons.
