body:
With the Ravens, Eagles and other teams potentially searching for help, we rank 10 quarterbacks who could be available before the Nov. 10 deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026 NFL trade deadline is fast approaching, and already some major deals have come down across the league. For instance, the Chicago Bears just made a blockbuster trade, sending multiple picks (including two first-rounders) to the Tennessee Titans for star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks also landed All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with Indianapolis. Those deals may have been the first, but there will certainly be more before the Nov. 10 deadline. Most of the conversation surrounding the deadline has largely centered around pass rushers, running backs and wide receivers. That said, the quarterback market could also heat up as a few teams across the NFL could be on the hunt for a signal caller. That includes both the Baltimore Ravens and Philadelphia Eagles, who each lost their starting quarterbacks. Then, there's the Minnesota Vikings, who could also eye an upgrade at the position with Kyler Murray struggling despite the team's 6-1 start to the year. With that in mind, we combed the market and identified 10 veteran quarterbacks who could be available for the right price on the trade market. 10. Joe Milton III
Milton is on the active roster of the Eagles after he was signed off of the Cowboys practice squad. He's backing up starter Tanner McKee, who ascended the depth chart in the wake of Jalen Hurts being put on the shelf with blood clots in his lungs. While Philadelphia would lose some depth at the position, Howie Roseman could see shipping away Milton as an opportunity to continue gaining future draft capital, albeit in the Day 3 range. 
The 26-year-old was a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024 out of Tennessee and spent his rookie season in New England before he was traded to Dallas in the spring of 2025. He's appeared in five games over the course of his career (one start) and has completed 69.8% of his passes for a 90.4 career passer rating. Milton is still raw, but has ability that could make him an intriguing addition. 9. Case Keenum
Keenum has started games this year for Chicago, so while he may be 38, he has recent starting experience that could be useful for a team looking for a QB. After Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent got hurt for the Bears earlier this year, Keenum started the club's Week 3 matchup against Philadelphia and impressed. He completed 24-of-34 (70.6%) for 247 yards and two touchdowns, while adding another score on the ground in a 27-7 win over the Eagles. Keenum also saw some action in Week 5, but the results were not as prolific, completing 11-of-19 for 108 yards and an interception. Still, he's shown an ability to come in and play at a serviceable level, which is really all you can ask for at this time of the year when searching for a quarterback. 
8. Andy Dalton
Dalton is another notable name who could be had, as he's in a crowded quarterback room with the Atlanta Falcons. The 39-year-old began the year with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was released by the team on Oct. 9. He then signed on with the Falcons, who released Cooper Rush to make room for him on the roster. Dalton is currently in a quarterback room that consists of starter Michael Penix Jr., Tua Tagovailoa, and undrafted rookie Jack Strand. Dalton made a brief appearance in the Eagles' Week 3 loss to the Bears, attempting one pass that was intercepted. While that doesn't exactly instill a ton of confidence, Dalton is a seasoned veteran who has 16 years and 169 career starts under his belt. 7. Anthony Richardson
The Colts are blowing it up. They already traded away Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and Jonathan Taylor seems like he could be next if the price is right. If Indy is willing to move that caliber of player, trading Anthony Richardson for any sort of return should be on the table even after benching Daniel Jones late in the Week 8 loss to Jacksonville. 
Richardson has been a bust so far for the Colts after they selected him with the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Florida. The 24-year-old is 8-7 as a starter and has a career completion percentage of 50.9% to go along with a 68.0 career passer rating. His raw ability and untapped potential could be of interest for a QB-needy team wanting to pick up a lottery ticket. For a rebuilding team like Indianapolis, extracting any value on the roster -- particularly for a player like Richardson, who is going to be a free agent this offseason --  makes too much sense. 6. Jameis Winston
Winston is the backup in New York after he lost the starting job to J.J. McCarthy. After Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury, Winston initially got the nod and the 12-year veteran largely struggled, despite a 2-1-1 record as the starter. He completed 57% of his throws and had seven passing touchdowns to go with five interceptions over six games played. Most notably, Winston's arm strength appeared diminished, which helped pave the way for McCarthy -- who they acquired in a trade with Minnesota -- to leapfrog him on the depth chart. While Winston may be past his prime, he's started 13 games over the past three seasons, so he's not the coldest quarterback on the market.  
5. Gardner Minshew
Minshew might be the new QB1 in Arizona, which could eliminate him from this list. However, the Cardinals should eventually see what they have in rookie Carson Beck, so if they can get value for someone like Minshew, it'd be negligent not to pull the trigger. After coming in for the benched Jacoby Brissett, Minshew helped lead Arizona to a fourth-quarter rally against the Cowboys and pulled off the upset win in overtime. The veteran completed 17-of-23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns in the winning effort. The 30-year-old began his career as a sixth-round pick of the Jaguars in 2019 and has bounced around the league since being traded out of Jacksonville in 2021. In all, Minshew has made stops in Philadelphia, Indianapolis, Las Vegas, and Kansas City before arriving in Arizona, so he is no stranger to jumping into new systems. He's started 47 games over the course of his career and is 17-30 as a starter. 4. Jacoby Brissett
Brissett could be one of the quarterbacks who is truly available on the trade market, especially after he was benched for Minshew against Dallas last week. The 33-year-old started the first eight games of the season for Arizona, owning a 3-5 record while completing 63.3% of his throws and a 79.7 passer rating. Brissett started 12 games for the Cardinals last year and had a 94.1 passer rating, so his production has slipped rather dramatically in 2026, which has since led to him finishing that Week 8 victory on the bench. 
If Arizona is going to turn the keys over to Minshew, it makes Brissett expendable, especially with rookie third-round pick Carson Beck waiting in the wings. Brissett has started in 73 games over the course of his career and is 23-50 in those contests. 3. Tyson Bagent
Caleb Williams is back healthy, which could make Bagent expendable. He was initially the top backup when Williams went down with a hamstring injury earlier this year, but had to give way to Case Keenum as the Week 3 starter after he landed in concussion protocol. Once he was cleared, Bagent did get the nod in Week 4 against New York, where he completed 25-of-34 for 268 yards and an interception.  The following week, he started against the Packers, but was eventually benched for Keenum after completing 57.1% of his throws and two interceptions. If Chicago feels comfortable with Keenum serving as the primary backup to Williams, Bagent becomes an intriguing trade chip as he's only 26 years old. 
2. Kirk Cousins
Cousins' future in Las Vegas is directly linked to the development of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. If the Raiders believe the rookie is ready to ascend atop the depth chart, Cousins becomes expendable on the trade market and maybe the most sought-after quarterback this deadline. After all, he's 4-4 as the Raiders starter, has thrown 19 passing touchdowns, and has a 101.4 passer rating through eight starts. He's had at least two passing touchdowns in seven of his eight games played this season. In the right situation, Cousins could help a reeling team -- like Baltimore, who just lost Lamar Jackson due to a right thumb injury -- stay afloat in the playoff race. 1. Mac Jones
It's unlikely that he's moved, but if you're ranking veteran quarterbacks who could be traded by the deadline, you have to at least mention Jones. He's arguably the top backup in the NFL, and given how well he filled in for Brock Purdy last year, the Niners would likely need to be blown away to deal him. 
In eight starts last season, Jones owned an 8-3 record while completing 69.6% of his throws and averaging 268.9 passing yards per game. He also had a 97.4 passer rating. The former first-round pick has been mentioned in trade rumors in the past, but San Francisco has held a high price, and it's hard to imagine they'd budge now. Still, if a team is looking to truly make a splash, he would likely be atop their wish list.

        A new college basketball season has arrived. The 2026-27 women's basketball campaign kicked off Sunday as Notre Dame took down Villanova in Rome. Most teams, though, are getting their seasons started on Monday and Tuesday.JuJu Watkins is back, UCLA enters are defending champs and South Carolina comes into the season as the nation's No. 1 team.
        
            
                JuJu Watkins returns after 588 days: USC star on family, the ACL tear and why 'there is no if' for the Trojans
                
                    Erica Ayala                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
So what should we expect this season? We're predicting the 2027 Final Four, the national champion and the National Player of the Year below.Final Four + title picks

            NPOYSarah StrongSarah StrongExpert explanationsGibbs: I know that there are no sure things in college sports anymore, but UConn and South Carolina making it to the Final Four is about as close as it gets. Both teams lost some key pieces last year – most notably Azzi Fudd and Raven Johnson to the WNBA – but are still incredibly stacked. UConn has the returning national player of the year, Sarah Strong, as well as veteran players like KK Arnold, Jana El Elfy and Ashlynn Shade. The Huskies are also adding Olivia Vukosa, the No. 2 player in the class per ESPN, and have sophomore Blanca Quiñonez back and ready to take on a bigger role.
There are a few more questions for USC, but mainly because the Trojans haven't made a Final Four since 1986. But they did make the Elite Eight in 2024 and 2025, and have the most talented roster of Lindsay Gottlieb's tenure. Not only is JuJu Watkins back after 588 days away due to her ACL injury, but she's joining the 2025-26 Freshman of the Year, Jazzy Davidson, and the No. 1 recruit from the class of 2026, Saniyah Hall. This should be a Final Four team at last.The fourth team was tough to choose – Michigan, LSU, Texas, Vanderbilt, even Notre Dame are all in the mix of about 10 teams I'd consider for this spot. However, I went with Duke. Kara Lawson's squad is coming off of back-to-back Elite Eight appearances, and added the No. 4 recruiting class and Texas Transfer Aaliyah Crump to the mix. I'm expecting Toby Fournier to be in the National Player of the Year conversation and both Arianna Robinson and Riley Nelson to take big steps forward. Plus, redshirt freshman Emilee Skinner – who Lawson was bullish about ahead of the 2025-26 season before Skinner's injury interrupted it – is finally healthy. The two-time defending ACC champions are ready to take the next step.Ultimately, though, I'm picking the Gamecocks as the national champions. Dawn Staley's team was outclassed in the title game by UConn in 2025 and UCLA in 2026, and she is not going to let that happen again. The depth in Columbia is staggering. Tessa Johnson, Agot Makeer and Joyce Edwards are back from last year's team; Chloe Kitts and Ashlyn Watkins, who both missed the entire season last year are back in the mix; Jordan Lee, one of the top guards in the portal from Texas, has joined the team; Alicia Tournebize, the 6-foot-7 Frenchwoman who only joined the Gamecocks for the second half of last year is ready to shine and, oh yeah, the No. 4 recruit, Oliviyah Edwards, and No. 6 recruit, Jerzy Robinson, are in town, too. While there is a little bit of concern over the lack of starting point guard experience, by March I'm sure Staley will have that problem solved. In fact, I think her biggest problem will be how to find enough minutes for that much top-level talent. I can't see any team having the depth and dynamism to keep up.

        
            
                Ranking the 10 best women's college basketball players for 2026-27: Can anyone catch Sarah Strong?
                
                    CBS Sports Staff                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Maloney: South Carolina, UConn and USC appear to be in a class of their own to start the season, and were easy picks to make the Final Four. It was much more difficult to decide on a fourth team to round out that prediction. Ultimately, I went with Texas. The Longhorns lost a lot of talent, but still have Madison Booker and brought in the top recruiting class in the country, per 247 Sports. Plus, Vic Schaefer always has his teams ready to compete in March. But Duke, LSU, Michigan and Vanderbilt all have a real chance to crash the party.Of that group, I'll take South Carolina to win the title after back-to-back runner-up finishes. Despite losing three players from last season's team to the WNBA, the Gamecocks have an absurd amount of depth, especially in the frontcourt with the return of Chloe Kitts and Ashlyn Watkins. If Tessa Johnson and Jordan Lee can solidify the backcourt, South Carolina will be the team to beat. On an individual level, I'll take Sarah Strong to repeat as National Player of the Year. She won it last season despite not being fully healthy and is the most versatile player in the country. Now that Strong is stepping into a bigger role without Paige Bueckers or Azzi Fudd alongside her, her numbers could be even better, and UConn is going to be one of the best teams in the country.

description: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Nov. 2
body:
Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Nov. 2

        Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!I have been watching the NFL for my entire life, and I have to say, yesterday might have been the most bizarre day in recent league history. We saw a team win a game with zero completions for the first time since 1974.We saw the Cowboys blow a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter at home for the first time ever.The Ravens became the first team in nearly 10 years to have three different quarterbacks throw a pass in the first half of a game.Trevor Lawrence pulled off a passing feat that the NFL hasn't seen in 55 years.We'll be covering all of this and more in today's newsletter, plus we'll have some picks and best bets for tonight's game between the Bears and Seahawks. As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here.  
1. NFL Week 8 grades: Raiders earn high mark with new look offense 
                                                                    Kathryn Riley/Getty Images
                                                            Welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter, which is where I hand out grades for all 32 teams. Actually, this week, I didn't grade all 32 teams because four were on a bye, and then we have two teams playing tonight, so you're only getting 26 grades.Raiders 38-33 over JetsRaiders takeaway: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak made it clear this week that Kirk Cousins was going to be his starter, and Cousins made his coach look like a genius for sticking with him. The Raiders QB was extremely sharp, especially in the red zone where the Raiders scored four touchdowns on four trips. Cousins accounted for all four scores with three TD passes and a rare TD run. The Raiders offense had an interesting new look with Mike Washington getting the brunt of the carries in the backfield. Ashton Jeanty had only two carries compared to 25 for Washington. With the Raiders performing well in the red zone and on third down — they went 7-of-11 — it won't be surprising if Washington continues to out-snap Jeanty going forward. The offense was clicking on Sunday with Kubiak's new plan. Grade: BJets takeaway: For the fifth time this season, the Jets lost a game by one score, and when that happens, it's usually a coaching problem. Aaron Glenn is a defensive-minded coach, but his defense couldn't stop anything in this game. The Raiders moved the ball at will, especially during the second half, when Vegas piled up 233 yards and 24 points. Offensively, the Jets were almost perfect: They became the first team this year to score on their first six possessions of the game. Adonai Mitchell had a career-high 142 receiving yards and Braelon Allen controlled things on the ground with 147 rushing yards, but it all comes back to the defense. You can't win in the NFL if you can't get any stops, and the Jets just couldn't get any stops. Grade: B-Broncos 28-24 over ChiefsChiefs takeaway: Harrison Butker might have just played his final game for the Chiefs. You can't blame this loss solely on him, but his missed kick in the fourth quarter set the stage for Denver's comeback win. It was a gut punch on a day when the Chiefs did almost everything right. Patrick Mahomes kept the Broncos' defense guessing by spreading the ball around: The Chiefs QB completed at least one pass to nine different players. That being said, Mahomes still needs some receiving help, as his top two receivers in this game were a tight end and a running back (Rookie Emmett Johnson led the team with 128 receiving yards). The defense pushed the Broncos around for three quarters, but then disappeared in crunch time. This is a good team, but it has plenty of flaws that have been exposed over the past two weeks. Grade: B-Broncos takeaway: This team looked to be left for dead in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs leading 24-13, but trailing big is apparently when Bo Nix is the most comfortable. Nix went 5-of-6 for 84 yards in the final quarter, including a 51-yard pass to Jonah Coleman that helped set up the go-ahead touchdown. From there, the defense did the rest. The Broncos pulled off an epic goal-line stand by stuffing the Chiefs on two straight plays from the one-yard line before ending the game with a sack. No one does fourth-quarter magic quite like the Broncos. It doesn't seem to matter how poorly this team plays in the other three quarters; they somehow find a way to win with the game on the line. Grade: BAs for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 8, you can check those out here. 


    2. NFL Week 8 winners and losers: Cowboys implode at homeYou can't have a week of NFL action without having winners and losers, so here are some winners and losers. I always get sad when there's a kicker on the loser's list, and yup, you guessed it, there's a kicker on the loser's list this week. 
Carter Bahns came up with this week's list of winners and losers, and we're going to check out his losers below. LOSERS Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer left his offense on the field on fourth-and-1 from his own 32-yard line in the first quarter, and the Cowboys turned the ball over on downs. That was the first sign that Sunday was not going to be their day. Coaching and offense failed them in that moment, and the defense failed them the rest of the afternoon, surrendering 33 points to the Cardinals in a stunning 33-30 overtime loss. The same defense that has not held a single opponent under 20 points all year, that is. Since 2000, the Cardinals were 1-174-1 when trailing by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter, and the Cowboys were 69-0 at home when leading by 14 or more in the fourth (according to ESPN Insights). If they cannot close out a game against that kind of opponent, then the Cowboys essentially cannot be trusted against anyone.Ravens' QB situation. To lose Jackson on his very first play back from a sprained ankle is the most cruel luck possible for a Baltimore offense that desperately needs him to stay healthy. The unit has not scored more than 13 points in any of its last three games, all losses. A team with Super Bowl aspirations now stands at .500 and in last place in the AFC North, and with Jackson out for at least four weeks as he undergoes surgery, it will be difficult to turn things around.Jim Harbaugh. The bye week would have been a sensible time for the Los Angeles Chargers to move on from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel after they finished their first six games as the NFL's lowest-scoring team. Instead, Jim Harbaugh stuck by his assistant, lauded his talent and then promptly watched as his unit managed a meager nine points in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Harbaugh has to own the fact that he could have made a play-caller change and that by not doing so, the offense continued to sputter. If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here. 3. Overreactions from Week 8: Is it time for the Vikings to bench Kyler Murray?  
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Everyone on the internet loves to overreact to things, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Personally, I overreact to everything. With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look at several things that happened during Week 8, so decide for yourself if we're all overreacting.  
Statement: Vikings should bench Kyler Murray.Overreaction or reality: Reality. I gave Murray a lot of grace early this year. He was on a new team and in a new system. He suffered a concussion moments into his Vikings debut. It was about as inauspicious a start as possible, and even as he struggled after he returned, I was willing to give him some time to figure it out. That time is over. Murray was dreadful again Sunday. Murray hasn't been close to good enough for a team with a championship-level defense, and Minnesota simply can't keep the status quo much longer.Statement: Colts should trade Jonathan Taylor and fire Shane Steichen.Overreaction or reality: Reality. Not trading Taylor would be a massive mistake. Indianapolis is facing a multi-year rebuild. They have no competent quarterback and likely no way to find one in the draft due to the Sauce Gardner trade. Taylor is reportedly commanding significant offers.     4. 15 crazy stats from Week 8: Buccaneers set football back 91 yearsEvery Sunday night, I get an email from our research department here at CBS Sports, and every Sunday, that email always includes some crazy stats about the games that were just played. With that in mind, here are 15 crazy stats from Week 8, with our main focus being on the Buccaneers' wild 16-0 win over the Falcons: Buccaneers win without completing a pass.
